title: Explain public publication and section subscriptions
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a reader and publication operator, I want feed documentation with usable examples, so that I can discover subscriptions and understand published updates.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Explain public publication and section subscriptions
  Scenario: Use documented subscriptions
    Given RSS and Atom delivery behavior has been implemented and verified
    When I follow its documentation
    Then I can discover publication and section subscription links and understand their scope
    And stable item identities, canonical links, published updates and withdrawals are explained
    And published-only visibility and freshness limits are explicit
    And planned endpoints are never represented as currently available
```

Documentation acceptance belongs to RSS epic; coordinate review with the Documentation overhaul. Avoid promising deletion from third-party caches or draft preview support.

Also document the approved automatic platform refresh after publish, saved published edits and unpublish: article, affected listings/indexes, sitemap and both RSS and Atom share current published selection/metadata. Explain private-draft isolation, freshness, known failed/pending ancillary outputs and supported retry/reconciliation. Link PPY-defff04e-17b5-4e28-9bb5-df412601a102; do not claim this new coverage is implemented or turn the guide into a single-site sitemap audit.

Approved dependency-guide correction: explain automatic extraction from supported declarative listing/embedded-content constructs at save/compile time and the generated reverse index. Rendering selection is the only source of type/featured parameters; no duplicated manual per-page rules. Cover union across components, old-or-new published-state matching for additions/removals/type/featured changes, and replacement/removal of stale page registrations. Publication visibility is enforced separately. Record unsupported custom-query fallback, exact extension ownership and schema syntax as open design questions. Anth.us main currently generates custom Python listing fragments and hashes them for incremental invalidation; do not present the proposed generic construct or reverse index as already implemented. See foundation PPY-3f55c3 and story PPY-defff0 for pinned source evidence.
